q.q: In calculations with respect to the position of the centre of gravity a reference is made to a datum. The datum is:

q.q: The arm is the ___ distance of a load as measured from the aircraft ___ .

o: Is a fixed point from which all balance arm distances are measured.

q.q: In mass and balance calculations which of the following describes the datum?
o: It is the point on the aircraft designated by the manufacturers from which all centre of gravity measurements and calculations are made.

q.q: An aircraft is used for Commercial Air Transport. Since the aircraft's initial entry into service, 3 years ago, several repairs and modifications have been executed. o: No, but it must be re-weighed within the next 12 months.

q.q: If all the moments are positive when calculating mass (weight) and balance, the position of the datum would be at the:
o: Nose, or forward of the aircraft.

q.q: The centre of gravity of an aircraft is that point through which the total mass of the aircraft is said to act. The weight acts in a direction:

Moment (balance) arms are measured from a specific point to the body station at which the mass is located. That point is known as:
The moment for an item is:
o: The mass of the item multiplied by its distance from the datum.

q.q: The weighing of an aircraft must be performed:
o: Whenever the cumulative change to the DOM exceeds plus/minus 0.5% of the MSLM.

o: 8.92 m aft of the datum line.

o: 83.7 in aft of the nose wheel.

q.q: In mass and balance calculations the 'index' is
o: A figure without unit of measurement which represents a moment.

o: a graphical reasoning to determine the CG position of operational masses.

Which of the following is unlikely to have any effect on the position of the centre of gravity on an aeroplane in flight?
o: Changing the tailplane (horizontal stabiliser) incidence angle.

q.q: When the centre of gravity is at the forward limit, an aeroplane will be:
o: Extremely stable and will require excessive elevator control to change pitch.

q.q: A load placed forward of the datum:
o: Has a negative arm and therefore generates a negative moment.

q.q: State the advantage(s) of the index method to determine moments.
o: It reduces the dimensions of the moments thus making it easier to calculate.

q.q: Which equation is correct in order to calculate the centre of gravity? The sum of the:
o: Moments divided by the sum of the masses.

Unfortunately, the ground staff incorrectly loaded all the cargo into the forward cargo hold. If the distance between the cargo holds ls 517 inches, is the aeroplane's CG within limits?
o: No, it is out of the forward limit.

q.q: During the pre-flight, the pilot assumed that the only passenger weighing 170 lb would sit at the front-row seat (located 85 inches aft of datum). The calculations gave a Take-Off Mass of 4100 lb and a take-off CG located at 94 inches aft of datum. When the passenger arrives, he/she sits at the rear seat, located 158 inches aft of datum. The CG limits are from 86 inches to 95 inches aft of datum. Determine if the new CG within limits:
o: No, it is out of the rear limit.

q.q: An aeroplane weighing schedule indicates that: The Empty Mass is 57 320 kg. The nominal Dry Operating Mass (DOM) is 60 120 kg. The Maximum Zero Fuel Mass (MZFM) is given as 72 100 kg. Which of the following is a correct statement in relation to this aeroplane?
o: Operational items have a mass of 2800 kg and the maximum Traffic Load for this aeroplane is 11 980 kg.

q.q: An aeroplane weighing schedule indicates that: The Empty Mass is 57 320 kg. The nominal Dry Operating Mass (DOM) is 60 120 kg. The Maximum Zero Fuel Mass (MZFM) is given as 72 100 kg. Which of the following is a correct statement in relation to this aeroplane?
o: Operational items have a mass of 2800 kg and the maximum Traffic Load for this aeroplane is 11 980 kg.

q.q: When must the centre of gravity (CG) be computed?
What are the effects of a CG forward of the forward limit?
o: Range, endurance and absolute ceiling will decrease.

q.q: What are the advantages of using the index method to determine moments? It:
o: Reduces the magnitude of moments, making it less time-consuming to compute.

q.q: Which of the following would not affect the position of the CG?

o: The final load sheet provided by the ground handler.

o: The Index at ZFM is within limits and in an aft position.

q.q: The principle of the index method is:
o: To divide high magnitude moments by a constant and thereby simplify calculations by decreased values.

Shipment W: 500 kg on a pallet sized 2 m x 2 m Shipment X: 500 kg on a pallet sized 1 m x 1 m Shipment Y: 600 kg on a pallet sized 2 m x 2 m Shipment Z: 600 kg on a pallet sized 3 m x 3 m (All pallets are in direct contact with the cargo floor).

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? Mark all correct answers.
o: Aeroplanes that have the most demanding airworthiness requirements have the least stringent operating regulations.
Aeroplanes that have the least stringent airworthiness requirements have the most stringent operating requirements.
To achieve a sufficient level of safety, the aeroplane performance required of commercial air transport aircraft may limit the weight of a dispatched aeroplane.
Single-engine Class B aeroplanes have the least stringent airworthiness requirements.

Performance Class A covers multi-engined aeroplanes powered by turbo-propeller engines with an MOPSC of more than 9 or a maximum take-off mass exceeding 5700 kg, and all multi-engined turbo-jet powered aeroplanes.
The minimum level of safety required for commercial air transport is ensured through the combination of airworthiness requirements and operational limitations.

q.q: The average for the aeroplane achieved by experienced and highly skilled test pilots' is a description of:

Which of these statements about safety factors is/are correct? Mark all correct answers.
o: The size of a safety factor depends on the likelihood of the event.
The size of the actual safety factor is affected by the range of the performance data.
The greater the probability of an event (greater than 1 in 1 million), the larger the safety factor required.
The safety factor for landing (67% for a jet) is much larger than for the all-engine take-off safety factor because of the much wider range of take-off performance.

q.q: An obstacle-free rectangular area on the ground at the end of the runway, at least the same width as the associated runway and centred along the runway’s centreline' is a description of:
The landing distance available is best described as:
o: The length of the runway from threshold to threshold.

The distance between the point on the surface of the aerodrome at which an aeroplane can begin its take-off run to the nearest point, in the direction of take-off, at which the surface of the aerodrome is incapable of bearing the weight of the aeroplane.
The distance between the point of touch down on the runway and the point on the runway where the aeroplane has come to a complete stop.

q.q: The take-off distance available (TODA) is normally:
o: The runway plus the clearway. The TODA is the lesser of: TORA plus clearway, or 1.5 times TORA.
The runway plus stopway. The TODA is the lesser of: TORA plus stopway, or 1.5 times TORA.
The runway plus stopway and clearway.
The runway plus the clearway. The TODA is the lesser of: TORA plus clearway, or 0.5 times TORA.

q.q: The distance between the point on the surface of the aerodrome at which an aeroplane can begin its take-off run to the nearest point, in the direction of take-off, at which the surface of the aerodrome is incapable of bearing the weight of the aeroplane under normal operating conditions' is a description of:

The distance from the point on the surface of the aerodrome at which an aeroplane begins its take-off roll to the nearest point in the direction of take-off at which it can’t roll over the surface of the aerodrome and be brought to rest in an emergency without risk of accident' is a description of:
Which of these statements about aerodrome distances is/are correct? Mark all correct answers.
o: The TORA often (but not always) corresponds to the physical length of the prepared and maintained runway pavement.
The TODA is the lesser of: TORA plus clearway, or 1.5 times TORA.

ASDA, TODA, and LDA are normally shown on Jeppesen aerodrome charts.
The TORA always corresponds to the physical length of the prepared and maintained runway pavement.

q.q: Which of these statements about energy transfer is/are correct? Mark 2 correct answers.
o: Between the start of the take-off to the end of the landing, all the potential energy and kinetic energy acquired by an aeroplane is ultimately derived from the chemical energy stored in the fuel.
By the end of the landing roll, all the potential energy acquired by an aircraft in flight has been lost to drag, heat and friction.
All the potential energy and kinetic energy acquired by an aeroplane is ultimately derived from the heat energy of the jet engine(s).
To minimise fuel consumption, a continuous descent is usually flown with the engines at flight idle, and speed brakes deployed to control the aeroplane's speed.

q.q: The most likely causes of arriving high and fast at the bottom of descent are: Mark all correct answers.
o: Failing to enter into the FMC accurate winds for the descent.
Failing to monitor closely the predicted bottom of descent position (the green banana).
Failing to calculate your height versus track miles to go.
Failing to plan the correct distance from the aerodrome for your top of descent.

q.q: Which of these statements about energy management is/are correct? Mark all correct answers.
o: If you are hot and high on the descent you may be able to add drag using spoiler and early stages of flap to correct the problem.
If you are hot and high on the descent, but you spot the problem very late in the descent, one option would be to ask ATC to increase the track miles to your descent point.
On a jet CAT aircraft, arriving hot and high at the start of the approach is potentially very dangerous.
On a jet CAT aircraft, arriving hot and high at the start of the approach can usually be corrected with speed brake, idle thrust and more flap.

q.q: The primary purpose of a continuous descent to final approach is to:
o: Minimise noise disturbance to people under the flight path.

q.q: Which of these statements about load-bearing surfaces is/are correct? Mark 2 correct answers.
o: The ACN gives a relative load rating of the aircraft on pavements for certain specified sub-grade strength.

The ACN for a pavement is the highest acceptable PCN for aeroplanes operating on the surface.
The PCN gives a relative load rating of the aircraft on pavements for certain specified sub-grade strength.

q.q: Which of the following statements about drag is/are correct? Mark all correct answers.

Parasite drag increases with TAS for a given density.
Induced drag decreases with an increase in TAS for a given density
The engine and warning display (EWD) is usually the upper central display.
The 2 main types of drag are parasite drag and form drag.

o: The component of weight, Wcosθ, is perpendicular to the flight path.

o: The angle of attack and coefficient of lift remain constant.

The induced drag steadily reduces, causing even greater acceleration.

The thrust steadily reduces with altitude.

q.q: The power created by a propeller: Mark 2 correct answers.
o: Drops at both ends of the speed spectrum because of reduced propeller efficiency.

o: Power available (PA) increases as TAS increases.
Thrust remains broadly constant across a wide speed range.
Ram effect offsets the rise in intake momentum drag.

q.q: What is “Surface wind”?

o: Veers in the friction layer and veers above the friction layer.

How does the height of the tropopause normally vary with latitude in the northern hemisphere?
o: It decreases from south to north.

q.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the temperature at the tropopause?
o: It is higher in polar regions than in equatorial regions.

q.q: Which is true of the temperature at the tropopause?
o: It separates the troposphere from the stratosphere.

q.q: Which one of the following statements applies to the tropopause?
When flying in warm air (warmer than standard atmosphere), indicated altitude is:
The QFF at an airfield located 400 metres above sea level is 1016 hPa. The air temperature is 10 °C higher than a standard atmosphere. What is the QNH?
o: Part of the atmosphere below the tropopause.

q.q: The troposphere is the:
o: Part of the atmosphere below the tropopause.

q.q: A polar low is a:
o: Small depression over sea areas, accompanied by frequent wintry showers.

q.q: The region of the atmosphere which is normally stable and has few clouds is known as the:
Choose the correct statement regarding the transfer of heat in the atmosphere:
o: The air at the surface can be cooled or warmed by the process of conduction, which is the molecular transfer of heat between the surface and the air in contact with it.

q.q: Although the large-scale structure of atmospheric circulation varies from year to year (e.g. El Niño/La Niña events), the basic structure remains fairly constant because it is determined by:
o: The Earth's rotation rate, the passage of air from high to low pressure, and the unequal heating of land and sea.

q.q: An aircraft flies from London to South France and experiences a strong wind from the left. Which of the following is correct?

Which of the following are valid countermeasures for avoiding or countering in- flight turbulence (mark all correct answers)?
o: To avoid CAT, track clear of strong, curved jet streams.
Avoid flying in the friction layer if possible.
Fly higher than, and upwind of, mountains.
At very high altitude, try to avoid climbing to escape turbulence.

q.q: Potentially the most dangerous form of windshear is:
Which of the following meteorological conditions is/are associated with a threat of low level windshear?
o: Large structures close to the final approach path, upwind.
A large heavy aircraft in front of you on the final approach.

q.q: Which of the following is associated with high level windshear (mark all correct answers)?
o: Aircraft on the same track as you and ahead of you.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are true (mark all correct answers)?
o: Downbursts are associated with strong, active, convective weather.
The only safe countermeasure to downbursts is to avoid them completely.

Downdraft speed is reduced by evaporation within the cloud.

q.q: The conditions necessary for forming mountain waves are (mark all correct answers):
o: Wind speed at mountain height must be at least 15–20 kt, increasing with height.
The wind direction must be within 30° of the perpendicular to the range of hills/mountains.
There must be a region of marked stability (an inversion or isothermal layer) at mountain top height with less stable air above and below.
There must be a region of marked instability at mountain top height with stable air above and below.
The wind direction must be within 90° of the perpendicular to the range of hills/mountains.

q.q: Which of the following statements about mountain waves is/are true (mark all correct answers)?
o: Underneath the first wave crest and in particular in breaking waves, severe up and downdrafts can occur.
Mountain waves start at the level of the mountain ridge line.
Mountain waves can propagate up to the tropopause.
